source_artifact.note: Timed-linked artifact; structured-event portion completed before later notable-work enrichment hit Wikimedia rate limiting.

task: Predict the domain of the next observed structured life event after age cutoffs 18/25/30/40.
split: 20 repeated 75/25 GroupShuffleSplit by person; a person never appears in both train and test in the same repeat.
interpretation: The reality-history baseline is clearly strongest in this first task.
Adding compact BaZi features reduces out-of-sample performance in every one of the 20 person splits.
Real BaZi features perform only slightly above decade-stratified shuffled-BaZi placebos on average; this is weak and inconsistent evidence, not a validated predictive signal.
BaZi-only modestly exceeds raw birth variables on average, but the difference is small and unstable.
The correct current conclusion is: no useful incremental BaZi signal has been demonstrated yet.
limitations: Observed Wikidata event sequences are strongly affected by biography/documentation bias.
Notable people are not representative of the general population.
The target is next documented event domain, not the true next life event.
Current splits are person-group random; forward-era and geography holdouts are still required.
Biography-text and notable-work enrichment were not included in this benchmark.
